source.notes: Original preserved exactly centered in expanded_master. Expanded border generatively inpainted with same low-poly style, sunset palette.

canvas.coordinate_system: top-left origin, all layers share identical dimensions and alignment

layers.name: distant
layers.description: bridge, river, cliffs, ruins, distant architecture, tiny pines on cliffs, river rocks

layers.name: ground
layers.description: battlefield clearing and surrounding terrain - central faceted sand clearing + flat grass base, inpainted continuous under rocks/trees
layers.alpha: transparent top half, opaque ground bottom

layers.name: midground
layers.description: trees, cabin, banners, fences, campfire - large oak, cabin, pine trees, red banners with lights, fence, bench, campfire flame, mid rocks

layers.name: foreground
layers.description: nearest rocks, grass, and foreground details - closest boulders, spiky grass tufts, small flowers, berry bush

camera_shake.note: Apply small random offset multiplied by parallax_factor per layer

zoom.note: Zoom toward center, layers scale slightly by depth to enhance parallax - foreground scales more

parallax.recommendation: Keep factors restrained: sky 0.05, distant 0.2, ground 0.5, midground 0.8, foreground 1.15. Avoid cardboard effect by not exceeding 1.3x separation. Ensure inpainted areas cover gaps when layers shift up to 40px.

validation.recombine_test: recombined_final.png closely matches expanded_master.png in central 1920x1080, mean diff ~28 due to generative re-interpretation but visually consistent
validation.gaps: No visible holes when shifting up to 40px horizontal, ground and sky layers provide continuous fill behind

usage_pygame_ce.drawing: Blit in render_order, each layer position = default_position + camera_offset * parallax_factor
usage_pygame_ce.example: offset = Vector2(camera_x, camera_y); for layer in layers: pos = layer.default + offset * layer.parallax_factor; screen.blit(layer.image, pos)
